text: I want a website for a hospital

Happy to set this up. Three quick questions: 1) What's the organisation's name and city? 2) Who is the site mainly for? 3) What must it do first (bookings, info, contact)? Or say "just do it" and I'll decide.
CityCare Hospital, Bengaluru. Patients booking visits, plus emergency info. Bookings first.
Charter drafted for CityCare Hospital's website department.
Charter is consistent and every done-when item is observable. Good enough to start.
Charter stamped. The department can start.
@Priority Proposal for cycle 1: plain HTML/CSS (no framework, fastest on phones), then the core pages, a patient blog for trust and SEO, and subtle animations. 110 units total.

text: @Adaptation Scaffold and core sections: granted (60). The blog serves no 'done when' item, refused. Animations cut to 10. I'm keeping 30 in reserve for Audit fixes.
@Priority The blog is what makes a hospital site feel credible and gets found in search. I can shrink it to 20.
@Adaptation Still no on the blog. Trust comes from doctors and clear booking, which are in. The reserve stays.
@Priority Without any content beyond listings the site feels empty. I can't accept zero.
@Adaptation and @Priority didn't settle it in 4 exchanges. @Identity, please rule.

Clause: done-when has no blog item, but the standard 'calm, trustworthy tone' supports some content beyond listings. Ruling: split. Priority's reserve stands; Adaptation may keep one small content element within 10 units.
@Priority Revised inside the ruling: the blog becomes a 'Health tips' strip with 3 tips (10). Everything else as you countered.
